article.story: LAHAINA, Hawaii -- — Nikola Dzepina led with 13 points and Lejuan Watts added 12 as Washington took down Clemson 64-63 in a Maui Invitational consolation game on Tuesday night. Watts was a perfect 6-for-6 from the field as Washington shot 47% as a team. Lathan Sommerville added 10 points and eight rebounds, and Ryan Beasley had nine points, six rebounds, and six assists. Though they only trailed for 19 total seconds of game time, the Huskies (5-1) weathered a late push by Clemson that brought the lead down to as few as two points. Washington built a double-digit lead in the first half thanks to a 10-0 run, and kept it a 10-point game at 33-23 heading into the locker rooms. The Tigers (4-3) continued to chip away and cut it to a two-point game with 57 seconds remaining in regulation. Washington's Steele Venters hit two clutch free throws with six seconds on the clock to clinch the victory, even as Ace Buckner hit a buzzer-beating 3-pointer. Buckner led the Tigers with 20 points (7-of-19 shooting) and had seven rebounds and five assists. Dylan Faulker scored 15 points and grabbed 11 rebounds, and Liutauras Lelevicius had 10 rebounds of his own. The Huskies have won all three meetings with the Tigers since 1982. Up next Washington: faces the winner of VCU-Colorado State in the fifth-place game on Wednesday.
